title: Consolidate chart control tokens and low-power rendering modes
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood's charting components have evolved organically: control buttons (zoom, pan, reset), small legend chips, and embedded tooltips currently pull colors, spacing, and motion settings from a mix of local variables and hardcoded values. This leads to inconsistent theming across consoles, surprises for product teams who toggle high-contrast or reduced-motion, and duplicate efforts when engineers tune performance for low-power devices.

Goal:
Create a small, well-documented token surface and a "reduced-power" rendering profile for time-series chart controls that: 1) centralizes token names and values for chart controls, 2) provides deterministic behavior for a11y modes (high-contrast, reduced-motion), and 3) enables an explicit low-power mode that engineers can toggle at runtime (pref key, media query, or component prop) for improved battery life and lower client CPU usage.

Scope / Includes:
- Define a set of CSS tokens scoped to chart primitives (buttons, icons, tooltip background/text, chip border, chip padding, axis-label-size). Example tokens: --chart-control-bg, --chart-control-fg, --chart-chip-bg, --chart-chip-border, --chart-tooltip-elevation, --chart-animation-scale.
- Author a short migration map from existing tokens/values used in ChartComponent, MiniLegend, and Tooltip to the new chart tokens.
- Design and document a "reduced-power" profile that: disables micro-animations, forces canvas fallback for heavy series, reduces sampling frequency (client-side decimation), collapses legend overflow into a single summarizing chip and defers non-essential DOM updates.
- Update Figma components for control buttons and micro-legend to reference design tokens and produce a token spec (light, dark, high-contrast).
- Provide acceptance criteria, a small dev kit snippet for engineers to toggle reduced-power, and two perf test scenarios (desktop baseline and low-power mobile).

Out of scope for this ticket:
- Server-side runtime batching changes (handled by ENG runtime teams).
- Full chart engine rewrites — we only add a conservative client-side profile and token mapping.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Token spec PR merged into design-tokens repo and published as a patch.
2) Chart control components (zoom, reset, legend chip, tooltip) consume new tokens with no visual regressions in light & dark.
3) Reduced-power profile implemented behind a feature flag and manually toggleable; reduces CPU spike in the mobile perf test by >= 30% in the synthetic harness.
4) Design spec (Figma) updated and linked from the component doc.
5) Accessibility checklist: high-contrast mode uses token overrides; reduced-motion respected when user prefers-reduced-motion is set.

Migration plan:
- Week 1: Finalize token list in design, create a migration mapping table for engineering.
- Week 2: Implement tokens in a small experiment branch, update Figma, validate visual parity.
- Week 3: Implement reduced-power flag and a minimal decimation strategy in the chart wrapper; run perf tests.
- Week 4: Ship as feature-flagged patch, monitor console dashboards for regressions, roll out to default after 1 week of metrics stability.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Token name collisions with existing global tokens. Mitigation: token naming convention uses chart- namespace and team review of token export.
- Risk: Reduced-power may hide important signals (annotations). Mitigation: reduced-power is conservative — annotation anchors are still shown, detailed overlays deferred but accessible via an explicit control.

Notes & references:
- Figma kit (WIP): https://www.figma.com/file/REPLACE-FIGMA-CHART-TOKENS
- Design tokens repo PR template: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/Design/Tokens+Guidelines
- Perf harness dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ChartPerf/low-power-tests
